components.note: 走 (run/walk) — relates to 越's meaning 'to exceed, cross over,' running past a boundary.
戉 (yuè) gives the sound — 越 is also pronounced yuè, an exact match.
Originally a pictograph of a musical bell or instrument hung in a frame; this shape was later reused to write the unrelated directional word 南, 'south.'

example.hanzi: 越南的咖啡很有名。
example.pinyin: Yuènán de kāfēi hěn yǒumíng.
example.english: Vietnam's coffee is very famous.
example.fact: Vietnam is the world's second-largest coffee producer after Brazil, and its output is dominated by robusta beans rather than the arabica more common elsewhere. Most of this coffee is grown in the Central Highlands region around Dak Lak province, where volcanic soil and a distinct dry season create ideal growing conditions. The country's coffee exports only took off after economic reforms in the late 1980s, transforming it from a minor producer into a global powerhouse within a couple of decades.

components.note: The traditional form 無 depicted a person holding tasseled decorations, likely from a ritual dance; the shape was later borrowed purely for its sound to write the unrelated word for negation, 'without, no.' The simplified 无 keeps only a reduced trace of that original picture.
见 (to see) — relates directly to 视's meaning 'to look at, view.'
礻 (a form of 示, shì) gives the sound — 视 is also pronounced shì, an exact match.

example.hanzi: 他完全无视了老师的警告。
example.pinyin: Tā wánquán wúshì le lǎoshī de jǐnggào.
example.english: He completely ignored the teacher's warning.
example.fact: The RMS Titanic received at least six iceberg warnings by wireless on the day it sank in April 1912, but several were never relayed to the officers on the bridge. The ship continued at near-full speed through the night despite the reports. Historians still debate how differently the crew might have acted had every warning reached the right hands in time.

meanings: to take a turn for the better

components.note: 女 (woman) — represents a mother.
子 (child/son) — a mother together with her child was seen as an image of goodness, giving 好 its meaning 'good.'
车 (cart) — relates to 转's meaning 'to turn, change direction,' like a wheel turning.
专 (zhuān) gives a sound hint — 转 is pronounced zhuǎn, sharing the same base sound with a different tone.

example.hanzi: 经过治疗,他的病情逐渐好转。
example.pinyin: Jīngguò zhìliáo, tā de bìngqíng zhújiàn hǎozhuǎn.
example.english: After treatment, his condition gradually improved.
example.fact: Alexander Fleming discovered penicillin somewhat by accident in 1928, after noticing that mold had killed the bacteria in a contaminated petri dish. It took over a decade, and the urgent needs of World War II, before scientists worked out how to mass-produce it. Once available, penicillin turned once-fatal bacterial infections into conditions from which patients could reliably recover.

components.note: A drawing of a person standing with arms and legs spread wide — used to represent the idea of something being 'big' or 'great.'
八 (to divide/split) — represents something being separated into smaller parts.
亅 (a hook/line) — cutting a small piece off, an image tied to the meaning 'small, tiny.'

example.hanzi: 这双鞋的大小正合适。
example.pinyin: Zhè shuāng xié de dàxiǎo zhèng héshì.
example.english: The size of these shoes fits just right.
example.fact: The blue whale is the largest animal known to have ever lived, reaching lengths of up to 30 meters and weights of nearly 200 tons. Its heart alone can weigh as much as a small car, and its calls can be louder than a jet engine. Even the largest dinosaurs, like Argentinosaurus, likely fell short of the blue whale in overall mass.

components.note: 衣 (clothing) — 装 relates to clothes, dress, and attire
壮 (zhuàng) gives the sound — 装 is pronounced zhuāng, a close match
亻 (person) plus 乍 (suddenly/for the first time) — together suggesting a person making or doing something for the first time.

example.hanzi: 她装作没看见我。
example.pinyin: Tā zhuāngzuò méi kànjiàn wǒ.
example.english: She pretended not to see me.
example.fact: Opossums really do "play dead" when threatened, a behavior called thanatosis. It is an involuntary, catatonic response rather than a conscious act — the animal's body goes limp, its breathing slows, and it can even release a foul odor to complete the illusion of a rotting carcass. The state can last anywhere from minutes to hours, and the opossum has no control over when it ends.

components.note: 片 (a slice/plate) — 版 originally referred to a wooden printing block
反 (fǎn) gives the sound — an exact match with 版's reading bǎn
木 (tree) — provides the base image of a tree.
一 (a line) marks the base of the trunk, highlighting the roots — giving 本 its meaning 'root, origin, source.'

example.hanzi: 这是软件的最新版本。
example.pinyin: Zhè shì ruǎnjiàn de zuìxīn bǎnběn.
example.english: This is the latest version of the software.
example.fact: Linus Torvalds released version 1.0 of the Linux kernel in March 1994, several years after he first announced the project as a hobby operating system in 1991. That kernel now underlies the vast majority of the world's servers, most smartphones through Android, and countless embedded devices. Its version numbering has continued steadily ever since, now well past version 6.

components.note: ⺮ (bamboo) — 管 originally referred to a bamboo pipe or tube, later broadening to mean 'to manage' or 'to control.'
官 (guān) gives a hint of the sound — 管 is pronounced guǎn, a connection that has shifted only slightly in tone.
辶 (to walk) — 道 relates to a path or road one walks along.
首 (shǒu) is the historical phonetic element; its modern reading no longer resembles dào, a reminder that sound components can drift after thousands of years of pronunciation change.

example.hanzi: 这条管道输送石油。
example.pinyin: Zhè tiáo guǎndào shūsòng shíyóu.
example.english: This pipeline transports oil.
example.fact: The Trans-Alaska Pipeline System, completed in 1977, stretches about 1,300 kilometers from the oil fields at Prudhoe Bay on the Arctic coast down to the ice-free port of Valdez. It crosses three mountain ranges and hundreds of rivers and streams along the way. Because much of the ground it crosses is permafrost, long sections of the pipeline are raised above ground on supports to prevent the pipe's heat from melting the frozen soil beneath it.

components.note: The oracle-bone form was a single vertical stroke, likely representing a knot tied in a rope as a simple way to count up to ten. Over time a horizontal stroke was added, producing the cross-like shape used today.
宀 (a house) — the setting for the scene.
子 (a child) — a child inside the house, perhaps evoking a name being nurtured, the source of 字's meaning 'character, word; courtesy name.'
木 (wood) — racks and frames like 架 were traditionally built of wood.
加 (jiā) gives a rhyme close to jià, with the tone shifted.

example.hanzi: 他脖子上戴着一个十字架。
example.pinyin: Tā bózi shàng dàizhe yí gè shízìjià.
example.english: He wears a cross around his neck.
example.fact: The Red Cross movement was founded in Geneva in 1863 by Swiss businessman Henry Dunant after he witnessed the aftermath of the Battle of Solferino. Its emblem, a red cross on a white background, was chosen simply by reversing the colors of the Swiss flag as a tribute to the country where the organization began. Dunant went on to receive the first Nobel Peace Prize in 1901.

components.note: 扌 (hand) — 接 relates to receiving or connecting something by hand.
妾 (qiè) gives a hint of the sound — 接 is pronounced jiē, a connection that has shifted over time.
⺮ (bamboo) — 管 originally referred to a bamboo pipe or tube, later broadening to mean 'to manage' or 'to control.'
官 (guān) gives a hint of the sound — 管 is pronounced guǎn, a connection that has shifted only slightly in tone.

example.hanzi: 新经理接管了这个部门。
example.pinyin: Xīn jīnglǐ jiēguǎn le zhège bùmén.
example.english: The new manager took over the department.
example.fact: The 1988 leveraged buyout of RJR Nabisco, in which KKR took over the food and tobacco conglomerate for roughly $25 billion, was the largest corporate takeover of its era. The battle for control, chronicled in the book "Barbarians at the Gate," involved rival bidding groups competing right up until the final vote by the company's board. For years afterward it remained the largest LBO ever completed.

components.note: The traditional form 亂 showed a hand at each end of a tangled skein of thread on a spool, an image of trying to sort out a disordered mess. The simplified 乱 keeps only a trace of that hand-and-thread arrangement, but retains the meaning 'chaotic, in disorder.'

The early form was written as a simple cross, close in shape to 十, and had no connection to any object — it was an abstract mark chosen to represent the number seven. A later, unrelated tradition reinterpreted the vertical stroke as bending, giving today's slightly hooked shape.
Two lines curving apart from each other, originally meaning 'to divide, split' — the shape was later adopted to represent the number 'eight.'
米 (grain, rice) — 糟 originally named the dregs left over from making rice wine.
曹 (cáo) gives a sound close to zāo, sharing the same rhyme and tone.

example.hanzi: 他的房间乱七八糟。
example.pinyin: Tā de fángjiān luànqībāzāo.
example.english: His room is in complete disarray.
example.fact: Meteorologist Edward Lorenz stumbled onto the idea now known as the butterfly effect in 1961, while re-running a weather simulation with a slightly rounded-off starting number. The tiny rounding difference produced a completely different forecast within a few simulated days. His finding helped launch chaos theory, showing that some systems are so sensitive to initial conditions that long-term prediction becomes practically impossible.

components.note: 衤 (clothing) — 被 originally meant a quilt or covering, like a blanket.
皮 (pí) gives a hint of the sound — 被 is pronounced bèi, a connection that has shifted over time.
宀 (a roof) sets the scene as something happening inside a home.
口 (a mouth) below the roof — harsh or slanderous words spoken within a household gave 害 its meaning 'to harm, injure.'
A simple line drawing of a person's legs seen from the side, used to depict a human being.

example.hanzi: 警方正在调查被害人的身份。
example.pinyin: Jǐngfāng zhèngzài diàochá bèihàirén de shēnfèn.
example.english: The police are investigating the victim's identity.
example.fact: Scotland Yard adopted fingerprint identification as an official crime-solving tool in 1901, based on a classification system devised by British official Edward Henry. It replaced the earlier Bertillon system, which relied on detailed body measurements and was far more error-prone. Fingerprint matching quickly became a cornerstone of criminal investigation worldwide and remains in wide use over a century later.

components.note: 缶 (a clay jar) — 缺 relates to something broken or missing, like a cracked vessel.
夬 (guài) reflects the character's historical phonetic root, though the modern reading quē has diverged.
少 depicts a few small dots or grains, like scattered sand — a simple picture of a small quantity, giving the meaning 'few' or 'little.'

example.hanzi: 这个计划缺少足够的资金。
example.pinyin: Zhège jìhuà quēshǎo zúgòu de zījīn.
example.english: This plan lacks sufficient funding.
example.fact: In 1747, Scottish naval surgeon James Lind ran one of the first controlled clinical trials in medical history, giving groups of scurvy-stricken sailors different remedies to compare. He found that the sailors who ate citrus fruit recovered dramatically faster than the others. Scurvy, it turned out, was caused by a simple lack of vitamin C, though it took the British navy decades to fully adopt citrus rations based on his findings.

components.note: 木 (wood) — 校 originally related to a wooden framework, later coming to mean 'school,' a place of structured learning
交 (jiāo) gives a sound close to 校's reading xiào
囗 (an enclosure) — a garden like 园 is an enclosed area of land.
元 (yuán) gives the sound — an exact match with 园.

example.hanzi: 学生们喜欢在校园里散步。
example.pinyin: Xuéshēngmen xǐhuān zài xiàoyuán lǐ sànbù.
example.english: Students like to take walks around the campus.
example.fact: Teaching is documented at Oxford as far back as 1096, making it the oldest university in the English-speaking world. It grew rapidly after 1167, when English students were banned from studying at the University of Paris and many returned home to study locally instead. Unlike many modern universities, Oxford has no single unified campus; its colleges are scattered as independent institutions throughout the city.

components.note: 扌 (hand) — 报 relates to taking action against someone.
卩 (a kneeling or bound person) — handling a wrongdoer and announcing the judgment gave 报 its meaning 'to report' or 'to announce.'
酉 (wine) — 酬 originally described toasting someone with wine.
州 (zhōu) gives a sound fairly close to chóu, sharing the rhyme.

example.hanzi: 他为这份工作要求更高的报酬。
example.pinyin: Tā wèi zhè fèn gōngzuò yāoqiú gèng gāo de bàochou.
example.english: He is asking for higher pay for this job.
example.fact: New Zealand passed one of the world's first national minimum wage laws in 1894, as part of the Industrial Conciliation and Arbitration Act. The law was meant to guarantee workers a baseline income and reduce the labor disputes that had become common in the country. It influenced similar legislation in Australia and, eventually, minimum wage laws adopted across much of the world in the twentieth century.

components.note: 力 (strength/force) — 动 relates to movement produced by exertion or force.
青 (blue-green, nature) — 静 relates to a calm stillness, like still water or clear skies
争 (zhēng) gives a sound distantly related to 静's reading jìng, having drifted apart over time

example.hanzi: 屋子里没有一点动静。
example.pinyin: Wūzi lǐ méiyǒu yìdiǎn dòngjìng.
example.english: There wasn't a sound in the room.
example.fact: Modern seismographs are sensitive enough to detect ground movements smaller than the width of an atom. This extraordinary sensitivity lets scientists register earthquakes from thousands of kilometers away and even pick up faint vibrations from ocean waves, wind, and distant traffic. The technology has advanced enormously since the first practical seismograph was built in the 1870s.

components.note: 攵 (a hand with a stick) — 教 relates to instructing or disciplining, the traditional action of teaching.
孝 (xiào) gives a hint of the sound — 教 is pronounced jiào, a connection that has shifted somewhat.
宀 (roof) — 室 refers to an enclosed room under a roof
至 (zhì) gives the sound — an exact match with 室's reading shì

example.hanzi: 老师走进了教室。
example.pinyin: Lǎoshī zǒu jìn le jiàoshì.
example.english: The teacher walked into the classroom.
example.fact: The University of Al Quaraouiyine in Fez, Morocco, founded in 859 AD, is recognized by UNESCO and the Guinness World Records as the oldest continually operating educational institution in the world. It began as a mosque with attached religious and legal instruction before formally becoming a university. Classes have continued there, with interruptions, for over eleven centuries.

components.note: 讠 (speech) — the act of speaking.
正 (straight, correct) — speaking the straight, correct truth, giving 证 its meaning 'to prove, certify; evidence.'
亻 (person) — 件 relates to a person separating something into parts.
牛 (ox) — dividing an ox into pieces gave 件 its meaning of an individual 'item' or 'piece,' now used as a measure word for objects and matters.

example.hanzi: 请出示您的证件。
example.pinyin: Qǐng chūshì nín de zhèngjiàn.
example.english: Please show your ID.
example.fact: Standardized passports as we know them largely date to a League of Nations conference in 1920, which recommended a common booklet format for international travel documents. Before that, passports varied wildly in size, format, and the information they contained from country to country. The basic booklet design recommended in 1920 still underlies the ICAO-standardized passports used almost everywhere today.

components.note: The oracle-bone form pictured a person bending over a basin of water to see their own reflection, since polished bronze mirrors had not yet become common. That act of close observation gave rise to 监's later meanings, 'to observe, supervise, monitor.'
示 (altar) — 禁 relates to sacred restrictions observed near an altar.
林 (lín) reflects the character's historical phonetic root, though the modern reading jìn has diverged.

example.hanzi: 他因盗窃被监禁三年。
example.pinyin: Tā yīn dàoqiè bèi jiānjìn sān nián.
example.english: He was imprisoned for three years for theft.
example.fact: Alcatraz Island's federal penitentiary operated from 1934 to 1963 in San Francisco Bay, holding notorious inmates such as Al Capone. Officially, no prisoner ever successfully escaped and survived, despite at least fourteen attempts across the prison's history. The fate of three inmates who vanished in a famous 1962 escape attempt, using a raft made of raincoats, has never been conclusively determined.

components.note: 灬 (fire) — 热 relates directly to heat
执 (zhí) gives a loose sound connection to 热's reading rè
灬 (fire) — 烈 relates to something as intense and fierce as fire
列 (liè) gives the sound — an exact match with 烈's reading liè

example.hanzi: 观众对表演报以热烈的掌声。
example.pinyin: Guānzhòng duì biǎoyǎn bào yǐ rèliè de zhǎngshēng.
example.english: The audience gave the performance enthusiastic applause.
example.fact: The 1883 eruption of the volcano Krakatoa in Indonesia produced what is often called the loudest sound in recorded history. It was clearly heard by observers roughly 3,000 miles away on the island of Rodrigues, near Mauritius, who described it as distant cannon fire. The pressure wave from the blast circled the entire globe multiple times, registering on barometers worldwide.

components.note: The traditional form 發 depicted a pair of hands drawing back a bow to shoot an arrow, the source of the meaning 'to shoot forth, send out.' That sense broadened over time to 'to issue, develop, occur,' and the simplified 发 preserves only a trace of the original bow-and-hand image.
口 (mouth) — with strokes above depicting a tongue sticking out — the image of speaking, the source of 言's meaning 'speech, words, language.'

example.hanzi: 代表们轮流上台发言。
example.pinyin: Dàibiǎomen lúnliú shàngtái fāyán.
example.english: The delegates took turns going on stage to speak.
example.fact: Abraham Lincoln's Gettysburg Address, delivered in 1863, lasted only about two minutes and roughly 270 words. Contemporary newspaper accounts noted that the crowd barely had time to react before Lincoln had already finished and sat down. Despite its brevity, it went on to become one of the most quoted speeches in American history.

components.note: The oracle-bone form has been interpreted as a bird flying up toward the sky; the meaning later shifted entirely to represent negation, 'not.'
Traditionally analyzed as 日 combined with 疋, linked to the idea of speaking directly and truthfully — the source of 是's meaning 'to be, indeed, right.'

example.hanzi: 这不是我的书。
example.pinyin: Zhè bùshì wǒ de shū.
example.english: This is not my book.
example.fact: Pluto is officially not a planet since 2006, when the International Astronomical Union adopted a formal definition of 'planet' that requires an object to have cleared its orbital neighborhood of other debris. Pluto shares its orbit with many other icy bodies in the Kuiper Belt, so it was reclassified as a 'dwarf planet.' The decision remains controversial among some astronomers even decades later.

components.note: The oracle-bone form showed a mouth issuing a command, an image tied to a ruler's authority, which gave rise to 后's older meaning 'queen, empress.' Since character simplification, 后 has also taken over the separate word 'after, behind' that was previously written with the unrelated character 後.
阝 (a mound/enclosure) — relates to 院's meaning 'courtyard, institution,' an enclosed place.
完 (wán) served as the phonetic base; its pronunciation has since drifted well away from yuàn.

example.hanzi: 孩子们在后院玩耍。
example.pinyin: Háizimen zài hòuyuàn wánshuǎ.
example.english: The children are playing in the backyard.
example.fact: In 1954, a meteorite crashed through the roof of Ann Hodges's home in Sylacauga, Alabama, bounced off a radio, and struck her while she napped on the couch. It remains one of the only confirmed cases in recorded history of a person being directly hit by a meteorite. Hodges suffered a large bruise but survived, and the rock is now known as the Hodges Meteorite.

components.note: 讠 (speech) — 谎 describes false speech, a lie.
荒 (huāng) gives the sound — an exact match with 谎, differing only in tone.
讠 (speech) — 话 relates to speaking and words.
舌 (tongue) — the organ used for speaking, reinforcing 话's meaning of 'speech' or 'words.'

example.hanzi: 他为自己编造了一个谎话。
example.pinyin: Tā wèi zìjǐ biānzào le yí gè huǎnghuà.
example.english: He made up a lie for himself.
example.fact: The modern polygraph, popularly known as the lie detector, was developed in the early 1920s by John Larson, a police officer and physiologist in California. It measures changes in heart rate, blood pressure, and skin conductivity that can accompany stress. Despite its long use in interrogations, courts in many countries have never fully accepted polygraph results as reliable scientific evidence.

components.note: The traditional form 無 depicted a person holding tasseled decorations, likely from a ritual dance; the shape was later borrowed purely for its sound to write the unrelated word for negation, 'without, no.' The simplified 无 keeps only a reduced trace of that original picture.
讠 (speech) — 论 relates to discussing or explaining something with words.
仑 (logical order, arrangement) — combined with speech, 论 came to mean 'to discuss' or 'a theory,' explaining ideas in an orderly way.
Traditionally analyzed as 日 combined with 疋, linked to the idea of speaking directly and truthfully — the source of 是's meaning 'to be, indeed, right.'

example.hanzi: 无论是晴天还是雨天,他都坚持跑步。
example.pinyin: Wúlùnshì qíngtiān háishi yǔtiān, tā dōu jiānchí pǎobù.
example.english: Whether it is sunny or rainy, he keeps running.
example.fact: The Mount Washington Observatory in New Hampshire recorded a wind gust of 372 kilometers per hour in April 1934, at the time the fastest wind speed ever directly measured by a person at Earth's surface. The mountain's summit sits at the intersection of several major storm tracks, making it one of the most consistently extreme weather locations in the world. Its record stood for six decades before being surpassed by a 1996 measurement during a tropical cyclone in Australia.

meanings: to throw sb to the ground

components.note: 扌 (hand) — 摔 involves a hand-related action of throwing down or a body falling.
率 (shuài) gives a sound close to shuāi, sharing the same initial and a similar rhyme.
亻 (person) — 倒 relates to a person falling over
到 (dào) gives the sound — 倒 is also pronounced dào, an exact match

example.hanzi: 老人在冰面上摔倒了。
example.pinyin: Lǎorén zài bīngmiàn shàng shuāidǎo le.
example.english: The elderly man fell on the icy surface.
example.fact: Falls are a leading cause of accidental injury and death among people over 65 in many countries, according to public health researchers. Part of the danger comes from simple physics: the friction coefficient of ice can drop below 0.05, far lower than the 0.5 to 0.8 typical of dry pavement, making it far easier to lose one's footing suddenly and without warning.

components.note: 讠 (speech, words) — the middle of the character, an exchange of talk.
辛 (bitter, sharp), placed on both sides, representing the two disputing parties, together giving 辩 its meaning 'to argue, debate.'
讠 (speech) — 论 relates to discussing or explaining something with words.
仑 (logical order, arrangement) — combined with speech, 论 came to mean 'to discuss' or 'a theory,' explaining ideas in an orderly way.

example.hanzi: 两位候选人展开了激烈的辩论。
example.pinyin: Liǎng wèi hòuxuǎnrén zhǎnkāi le jīliè de biànlùn.
example.english: The two candidates engaged in a heated debate.
example.fact: The first televised U.S. presidential debate took place on September 26, 1960, between John F. Kennedy and Richard Nixon. An estimated 70 million viewers tuned in, and many historians credit Kennedy's composed appearance on camera, compared with a sweating, underslept Nixon, with helping tip the close election in his favor. The debate marked a turning point in how television would shape political campaigns.

components.note: 亻 (person) — 仇 describes a person one holds a grudge against, 'an enemy.'
九 (jiǔ) is only distantly related in sound to chóu — the connection has drifted apart over time.
忄 (heart/mind) — 恨 describes a strong feeling in the heart, hatred.
艮 (gèn) gives a sound close to hèn.

example.hanzi: 这场战争源于多年的仇恨。
example.pinyin: Zhè chǎng zhànzhēng yuányú duōnián de chóuhèn.
example.english: This war stemmed from years of hatred.
example.fact: A 2008 study by researchers at University College London used brain scans to identify a distinct neural network activated when people view images of someone they hate. The pattern overlapped with regions of the brain, including the putamen and insula, that are also involved in generating aggressive behavior. The findings suggested that hatred, unlike simple anger, engages a somewhat unique combination of brain circuits.

components.note: 亻 (person) — 代 relates to a person's place in time.
弋 (a stake used to mark or catch something) — combined with 亻 (person), 代 came to mean a 'generation' or 'era,' and 'to take the place of' someone.
石 (stone) — 码 originally related to counting stones used for reckoning, extended to mean 'number, code.'
马 (mǎ) is an exact match for the sound of 码.

example.hanzi: 程序员正在检查这段代码。
example.pinyin: Chéngxùyuán zhèngzài jiǎnchá zhè duàn dàimǎ.
example.english: The programmer is checking this piece of code.
example.fact: The term 'bug' for a technical defect gained wide popularity in computing after a moth was found jammed in a relay of the Harvard Mark II computer in 1947, causing a malfunction. Engineers taped the moth into the logbook with the note 'first actual case of bug being found.' The word itself predates that incident by decades, but the anecdote helped cement it permanently into engineering culture.

components.note: Originally a drawing of a bear, with 厶 as its head, ⺼ as its body, and 匕匕 as its claws; the picture was later borrowed to mean 'ability, to be able to.'
氵 (water) — 源 originally referred to the spring where a river begins
原 (yuán) gives the sound — an exact match with 源's reading yuán

example.hanzi: 太阳能是一种清洁的能源。
example.pinyin: Tàiyángnéng shì yì zhǒng qīngjié de néngyuán.
example.english: Solar power is a clean source of energy.
example.fact: The sun converts roughly 4 million tons of its own mass into energy every single second through nuclear fusion, radiating about 3.8 x 10^26 watts in all directions. Earth intercepts only a tiny fraction of that output, yet it is still far more energy than humanity currently uses in a year. The conversion follows Einstein's famous relation E = mc², linking mass directly to energy.

components.note: A drawing of a person standing with arms and legs spread wide — used to represent the idea of something being 'big' or 'great.'
亻 (person) — 使 involves a person carrying out a task.
吏 (a government official) — 使 originally referred to an official sent to carry out orders, giving rise to the meaning 'to make someone do something' or 'to use.'

example.hanzi: 他被任命为驻美大使。
example.pinyin: Tā bèi rènmìng wéi zhù Měi dàshǐ.
example.english: He was appointed ambassador to the United States.
example.fact: Permanent resident embassies, rather than temporary diplomatic missions, are usually traced to the Italian Renaissance city-states. Milan is credited with sending one of the first known permanent ambassadors, to the court of Genoa around 1455. The practice spread across Europe over the following century, eventually becoming the standard model for diplomacy still used by nations today.

components.note: 页 (head) — relates to 领's meaning 'neck, collar; to lead,' the head/neck area.
令 (lìng) gives a sound hint — 领 is pronounced lǐng, sharing the same rhyme with a different tone.
儿 (child) — 养 relates to raising and nurturing children or animals
羊 (yáng) gives a sound close to 养's reading yǎng, sharing a similar historical pronunciation

example.hanzi: 他们决定领养一个孩子。
example.pinyin: Tāmen juédìng lǐngyǎng yí gè háizi.
example.english: They decided to adopt a child.
example.fact: Researchers studying emperor penguin colonies in Antarctica have documented cases of adult penguins 'adopting' chicks that are not biologically their own, typically after losing their own egg or chick earlier in the season. This behavior can sometimes turn competitive, with several adults attempting to claim the same stray chick at once. It remains one of the more striking examples of parental instinct persisting even without a genetic link.

components.note: 取 (a hand at an ear) — gathering information or people.
乑 (people standing side by side) — together giving 聚 its meaning 'to assemble, gather.'
隹 (a bird) — one of a flock.
木 (a tree) — birds flocking together on a tree, the image of gathering that gave 集 its meaning 'to gather, collect; a collection.'

example.hanzi: 人群在广场上聚集。
example.pinyin: Rénqún zài guǎngchǎng shàng jùjí.
example.english: A crowd gathered in the square.
example.fact: Globular star clusters such as Omega Centauri can contain up to 10 million stars, all gravitationally bound together within a region only about 150 light-years across. That packs an enormous stellar population into a comparatively tiny volume of space. Astronomers believe some globular clusters may even be the stripped-down cores of small galaxies that were absorbed by larger ones long ago.

meanings: Brooklyn, borough of New York City

components.note: 巾 (cloth) — held in a hand, the image behind 布's meaning 'cloth' and, by extension, 'to spread out, distribute.'
鱼 (fish) forms the top of the character.
日, placed beneath the fish, was linked to the idea of speaking crudely or bluntly, giving 鲁 its meaning 'rash, uncouth.'
十 (here representing a weapon or armor) — 克 pictures overcoming an opponent.
兄 (a person, here representing a formidable figure) — overcoming a strong opponent gave 克 its meaning 'to overcome' or 'to be able to.'
木 (tree), doubled — two trees side by side depict a cluster of trees, the source of 林's meaning 'forest, grove.'

example.hanzi: 他们去布鲁克林大桥散步。
example.pinyin: Tāmen qù Bùlǔkèlín Dàqiáo sànbù.
example.english: They went for a walk on the Brooklyn Bridge.
example.fact: The Brooklyn Bridge opened in 1883 after fourteen years of construction, connecting Manhattan and Brooklyn across the East River. At the time it opened, its main span of 1,595 feet made it the longest suspension bridge in the world. Its chief engineer, John Roebling, died from an infection following an injury sustained while surveying the site, and his son Washington Roebling oversaw the bridge's completion.

components.note: 田 here pictures the stomach itself, reused from its usual meaning 'field.'
⺼ (flesh) sits below, marking 胃 as a body part.
口 is a simple picture of an open mouth.

example.hanzi: 生病让他失去了胃口。
example.pinyin: Shēngbìng ràng tā shīqù le wèikǒu.
example.english: Being sick made him lose his appetite.
example.fact: The hormone ghrelin, discovered in 1999, is produced mainly by cells lining the stomach and is often called the 'hunger hormone.' Its levels rise sharply before a meal and drop again shortly after eating, signaling to the brain when the body needs fuel. Researchers have since found that ghrelin also affects mood, memory, and sleep, well beyond its original role in appetite.

components.note: 冂 depicts a boundary or border enclosing an area.
土 (earth/land) — the land enclosed within the border.
口 here depicts a well within that land — together giving 周 its early meaning of a bounded territory, and later 'circumference, week, the Zhou dynasty.'
二 is simply two horizontal strokes stacked together — the most direct way to picture the number two, following the same pattern as 一 (one) and 三 (three).

example.hanzi: 会议将在下周二举行。
example.pinyin: Huìyì jiāng zài xià zhōu'èr jǔxíng.
example.english: The meeting will be held next Tuesday.
example.fact: October 29, 1929, is remembered as 'Black Tuesday,' the day the New York Stock Exchange suffered its most devastating crash of the era. The Dow Jones Industrial Average lost about 12 percent of its value in a single trading session as panicked investors rushed to sell. The crash is widely seen as the event that triggered the decade-long Great Depression that followed.

components.note: 亻 (person) — 值 relates to worth or value assigned by a person
直 (zhí) gives the sound — 值 is also pronounced zhí, an exact match
钅 (metal) — 钱 relates to money, since early Chinese coins were made of metal
戋 (jiān) gives a loose sound connection to 钱's reading qián

example.hanzi: 这块古董非常值钱。
example.pinyin: Zhè kuài gǔdǒng fēicháng zhíqián.
example.english: This antique is extremely valuable.
example.fact: In 2017, a small Northern Song-dynasty Ru ware brush washer, barely larger than a teacup, sold at auction in Hong Kong for over 294 million Hong Kong dollars, roughly 37 million US dollars at the time. The sale set a record for Chinese ceramics, driven partly by the extreme rarity of surviving Ru ware, of which fewer than 100 complete pieces are known to exist worldwide.

components.note: 氵 (water) — relates directly to 流's meaning 'to flow.'
㐬 (liú) gives the sound — 流 is also pronounced liú, an exact match.
攵 (a hand with an implement, action) — relates to 放's meaning 'to let go, release, put.'
方 (fāng) gives the sound — 放 is pronounced fàng, a close match sharing the same rhyme.

example.hanzi: 那位诗人被流放到边疆。
example.pinyin: Nà wèi shīrén bèi liúfàng dào biānjiāng.
example.english: That poet was exiled to the frontier.
example.fact: Napoleon Bonaparte was first exiled to the small Mediterranean island of Elba in 1814 after his abdication, only to escape within a year and briefly return to power. Following his final defeat at Waterloo in 1815, he was exiled a second time, this time to the remote South Atlantic island of Saint Helena, where he lived under British guard until his death in 1821.

components.note: 着 developed as a simplified variant of 著, replacing the phonetic component 者 with 目 (eye) while keeping the grass radical 艹 reduced to a small mark on top. Its core sense, 'to touch, attach, arrive,' broadened into uses like 'to wear' and the grammatical particle marking an ongoing state.
心 (heart/mind) — 想 relates to thinking, missing someone, or wanting something in one's heart.
相 (xiāng) gives the sound — 想 is pronounced xiǎng, matching aside from tone.

example.hanzi: 父母总是为孩子着想。
example.pinyin: Fùmǔ zǒngshì wèi háizi zhuóxiǎng.
example.english: Parents always think of their children.
example.fact: The 'trolley problem,' a thought experiment introduced by philosopher Philippa Foot in 1967 and later expanded by Judith Jarvis Thomson, asks whether it is right to divert a runaway trolley to kill one person instead of five. It has since become a standard tool in psychology and neuroscience for studying how people weigh the interests of others when making difficult moral decisions. Variations of the problem are still used in research on self-driving car ethics today.

components.note: 哭 (to cry) — the top of the simplified character keeps the idea of crying in mourning.
亡 (dead, gone) — combined with crying above it, the image of weeping over the dead gave 丧 its meaning 'mourning, funeral.'
丿 (something falling) — an object slipping away.
夫 (a hand/person) — the object slipping out of a hand, giving 失 its meaning 'to lose.'

example.hanzi: 事故后,他丧失了部分记忆。
example.pinyin: Shìgù hòu, tā sàngshī le bùfen jìyì.
example.english: After the accident, he lost part of his memory.
example.fact: The patient known in scientific literature as H.M., Henry Molaison, lost the ability to form new long-term memories after undergoing experimental brain surgery in 1953 to treat severe epilepsy. Researchers studied him for decades afterward, and his case became one of the most influential in the history of memory research, helping establish that different brain regions handle different types of memory.

components.note: 雨 (rain) — 雪 belongs to the group of weather words built on 雨, since snow falls the way rain does.
彐 gives a sound distantly related to xuě, having drifted apart over time.
艹 (grass, plant) — 茄 (the eggplant) is a plant.
加 (jiā) gives the sound — an exact match with 茄's reading.

example.hanzi: 他喜欢在晚饭后抽雪茄。
example.pinyin: Tā xǐhuān zài wǎnfàn hòu chōu xuějiā.
example.english: He likes to smoke a cigar after dinner.
example.fact: Cuba's Pinar del Río province, particularly its Vuelta Abajo region, is widely regarded by tobacco experts as producing some of the finest cigar tobacco in the world. Its reddish clay soil, high humidity, and specific microclimate are considered difficult to replicate elsewhere. The region has supplied leaf for Cuban cigars for well over a century.

components.note: A short stroke placed above a longer one — a simple graphic way to show 'up' or 'above,' contrasted with 下 (down), which flips the strokes.
A drawing of a robe's collar and folded sides, seen from the front.

example.hanzi: 她穿了一件红色的上衣。
example.pinyin: Tā chuān le yí jiàn hóngsè de shàngyī.
example.english: She wore a red jacket.
example.fact: Gideon Sundback patented an improved version of the modern zipper in 1913, but it took another one to two decades before manufacturers widely adopted it for clothing such as jackets. Early marketing struggled because the zipper was seen mainly as a novelty for boots and tobacco pouches. It was only in the 1930s, after a push from the fashion industry, that zippers became a standard fastener on everyday garments.

components.note: A simple line drawing of a person's legs seen from the side, used to depict a human being.
忄 (heart/mind) — 性 relates to inner nature or character.
生 (shēng) gives a hint of the sound — 性 is pronounced xìng, a related sound though the initial has shifted.

example.hanzi: 这部电影深刻地探讨了人性。
example.pinyin: Zhè bù diànyǐng shēnkè de tàntǎo le rénxìng.
example.english: This film explores human nature deeply.
example.fact: The Stanford Prison Experiment, run by psychologist Philip Zimbardo in 1971, assigned college students to act as guards or prisoners in a simulated jail and observed how quickly ordinary people adopted abusive or submissive roles. The study was cut short after only six days due to the severity of the behavior it provoked. Decades later, historians and psychologists have raised serious questions about its methodology, but it remains widely cited in discussions of situational influence on behavior.

components.note: 米 (grain) — 粗 originally described coarsely hulled grain, extending to 'rough, coarse' in general.
且 (qiě) gives a sound distantly related to cū's reading, having drifted apart considerably over time.
鱼 (fish) forms the top of the character.
日, placed beneath the fish, was linked to the idea of speaking crudely or bluntly, giving 鲁 its meaning 'rash, uncouth.'

example.hanzi: 他对服务员的态度很粗鲁。
example.pinyin: Tā duì fúwùyuán de tàidù hěn cūlǔ.
example.english: His attitude toward the waiter was very rude.
example.fact: At the court of Louis XIV in seventeenth-century Versailles, strict rules of conduct were literally posted on small placards called 'etiquettes,' the origin of the modern word 'etiquette.' Nobles who violated the posted rules risked real social consequences, including loss of royal favor. The system reflected just how tightly regulated courtly behavior had become under the French monarchy.

components.note: 亠 — read as the head of an animal standing upright in this pictograph; the character was later reused for the unrelated meaning 'to leave, be apart from, distance.'
宀 (roof) — 家 is about a home, the space under a roof.
豕 (shǐ, 'pig') supplies the ancient sound for 家; keeping a pig under one's roof was also a practical sign of a household in ancient China, though the modern readings jiā and shǐ no longer rhyme.

example.hanzi: 他很小就离家去外地工作了。
example.pinyin: Tā hěn xiǎo jiù líjiā qù wàidì gōngzuò le.
example.english: He left home to work elsewhere when he was very young.
example.fact: The United Nations estimated that about 281 million people were living outside their country of birth as international migrants in 2020. A large share left home primarily in search of better economic opportunity, joining family members already abroad, or fleeing conflict. That figure has grown steadily for decades as global travel and communication have made moving away from home more feasible.

components.note: 口 (mouth) — relates directly to 叫's meaning 'to call out, shout; to be named.'
丩 (jiū) served as the phonetic base; its pronunciation has since drifted well away from jiào.
酉 (wine jar) — 醒 originally described sobering up from drink, extending to 'to wake up.'
星 (xīng) gives a sound close to xǐng, sharing the same syllable body and differing mainly in tone.

example.hanzi: 请明天早上七点叫醒我。
example.pinyin: Qǐng míngtiān zǎoshang qī diǎn jiàoxǐng wǒ.
example.english: Please wake me up at seven tomorrow morning.
example.fact: The snooze button was introduced on alarm clocks in the 1950s, and Westclox's 1956 'Drowse' model set the nine-minute snooze interval that became an industry standard. The odd length was reportedly chosen because of gear-ratio constraints inside the clock's mechanism rather than any particular psychological reasoning. That same nine-minute default still shows up on many digital alarm clocks and smartphones today.

components.note: 廾 (two hands) — depicts hands at work.
一 represents the latch or bar of a door; hands lifting it away gave 开 its meaning 'to open, to start.'
土 (earth) — 场 relates to a flat open area of ground, such as a field or venue.
昜 (yáng) gives a hint of the sound — 场 is pronounced chǎng, a connection that has drifted significantly over time.

example.hanzi: 演出的开场非常精彩。
example.pinyin: Yǎnchū de kāichǎng fēicháng jīngcǎi.
example.english: The opening of the show was spectacular.
example.fact: Cirque du Soleil, founded in Quebec in 1984, transformed circus performance by removing traditional animal acts entirely and building shows instead around narrative-driven acrobatics and original music. Its opening acts were designed to immediately immerse audiences in a specific theme or story, a sharp departure from the traditional ringmaster-led circus format. The approach helped the company grow from a small Canadian troupe into a global entertainment brand.

components.note: 车 (cart/wheel) — 辐 relates to parts of a wheel, the spokes.
畐 (fú) gives the sound — an exact match with 辐.
身 — depicts a drawn bow
寸 — a hand releasing the arrow

example.hanzi: 医生提醒他要小心辐射。
example.pinyin: Yīshēng tíxǐng tā yào xiǎoxīn fúshè.
example.english: The doctor reminded him to be careful of radiation.
example.fact: Marie Curie, who discovered the properties of radioactivity alongside her husband Pierre in the late 1890s, died in 1934 of aplastic anemia almost certainly caused by decades of radiation exposure. Her personal notebooks remain so radioactive that they are stored today in lead-lined boxes at France's national library, and visitors who wish to view them must sign a waiver and wear protective clothing.

components.note: A short stroke placed below a longer one — the mirror image of 上 (up), together forming a simple, opposite pair.
艹 (grass/plant) — 落 relates to leaves or plants falling
洛 (luò) gives the sound — 落 is also pronounced luò, an exact match

example.hanzi: 警方仍未查明失踪者的下落。
example.pinyin: Jǐngfāng réng wèi chámíng shīzōngzhě de xiàluò.
example.english: The police still haven't determined the missing person's whereabouts.
example.fact: Amelia Earhart disappeared over the Pacific Ocean in July 1937 while attempting to become the first woman to fly around the world. Despite numerous search expeditions in the decades since, including several well-funded modern efforts using sonar and underwater robots, her aircraft's final resting place has never been conclusively confirmed.

components.note: 艹 (grass/plant) — 落 relates to leaves or plants falling
洛 (luò) gives the sound — 落 is also pronounced luò, an exact match

The oracle-bone form showed a mouth issuing a command, an image tied to a ruler's authority, which gave rise to 后's older meaning 'queen, empress.' Since character simplification, 后 has also taken over the separate word 'after, behind' that was previously written with the unrelated character 後.

example.hanzi: 这个地区的经济发展相对落后。
example.pinyin: Zhège dìqū de jīngjì fāzhǎn xiāngduì luòhòu.
example.english: This region's economic development is relatively backward.
example.fact: Bhutan formally adopted a 'Gross National Happiness' framework into its constitution in 2008, using it alongside or instead of GDP to measure national progress. The index weighs factors such as psychological well-being, health, education, and environmental conservation rather than economic output alone. The approach has drawn international attention as an alternative way to think about what counts as development.

components.note: 巾 (cloth) — the bottom half of a belt, hanging straight down.
Above the cloth, the strokes crease as if folded at the waist — depicting a belt or sash, the source of 带's meaning 'belt, band,' later 'to bring, carry along.'
页 (head) — relates to 领's meaning 'neck, collar; to lead,' the head/neck area.
令 (lìng) gives a sound hint — 领 is pronounced lǐng, sharing the same rhyme with a different tone.

example.hanzi: 导游带领游客参观了故宫。
example.pinyin: Dǎoyóu dàilǐng yóukè cānguān le Gùgōng.
example.english: The guide led the tourists on a tour of the Forbidden City.
example.fact: The Forbidden City in Beijing was completed in 1420 during the Ming dynasty and served as the imperial palace for 24 emperors across the Ming and Qing dynasties. It contains 980 surviving buildings, making it the largest preserved palace complex in the world. The complex remained off-limits to ordinary citizens for nearly five centuries, giving rise to its English name.
